confidence_notes: I ran three searches: one for the RBA rate and two for food and drink. The food and drink sources disagreed and were dated differently. Inexpensive meals were about $5-10. Beer ranged from $1.77 to $4.95. Cappuccino ranged from $2 to $5.82. One spa café listed wine by the glass at $6-8 and mimosas and spritzes at $8. Midrange meal for two is a holistic estimate from tourist-oriented pricing, with no direct source. Cocktail is set at about 2x beer and wine from the spa café menu. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of this tourist town, with seasonal variation. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. Hostel and budget-room supply is thin, so those anchors are especially uncertain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Victoria Falls is a USD-priced, tourism-driven town. I based the estimates on its own search results and on similar safari gateway towns in southern Africa, such as Livingstone, Zambia, and Kasane, Botswana. Prices are higher than in the rest of Zimbabwe.
